description: Fleet release-gating and cadence policy for RIPDPI profile and fleet rollouts. Defines daily, weekly, release/rotation, staging, production, relay-deployment, and client-release gate sets, plus the no-ship and warn-only failure policy. This artifact is the machine-readable source of truth enforced by scripts/ci/check_fleet_release_gates.py. The release gate produces a short sanitized report; raw probe logs and live endpoints belong under ops/live-infra/, never here.

staging.description: Staging deploy gate set; must pass before a production deploy is allowed.

production.description: Production deploy gate set; every gate is a no-ship blocker for promoting a profile to a primary production path.

relay-deployment.description: Owner-operated relay deployment gate set; must pass before a relay endpoint or profile is promoted as an operator-managed path.

noShipPolicy.description: A FAIL on any no-ship condition demotes the profile or blocks the client release; it is never shipped as a primary path.

warnOnlyPolicy.description: A FAIL on a warn-only condition is reported as WARN: it does not block the release but is surfaced in the sanitized report so degraded paths are demoted rather than relied on as primary.

report.description: The release gate emits a short sanitized PASS/WARN/FAIL summary per gate set, never raw probe logs or live endpoints.

deploymentPlane.description: First-class operational controls for owner-operated relay and server paths. These controls are required for production relay promotion and are documented in docs/relay-deployment-operations.md.
deploymentPlane.redactionPolicy: Only sanitized PASS/WARN/FAIL summaries and stable control IDs are committed. Live endpoints, raw probe logs, private keys, client UUIDs, tokens, and provider account identifiers stay outside the repo.

evidence: new certificate chain served by staging before production promotion
old certificate no longer served on the promoted endpoint
expiry margin and issuer chain recorded in the sanitized report
revoked device credential fails to connect
profile export contains no revoked credential material
fresh relay instance reaches readiness from checked-in IaC or documented bootstrap inputs
new instance receives only intended listener and firewall state
old instance can be drained and destroyed without reusing host-local secrets
observed listener set matches the declared relay profile
provider firewall and host firewall rules match the expected allowlist
admin panels and metrics endpoints are not reachable from public networks
IP burn response is documented with demotion and replacement steps
credential leak response is documented with per-device revocation steps
certificate-expiry and firewall-drift responses are documented with rollback steps
